items.question: How do I calm down and wait on God so I can hear from Him?
items.text:
That's a good and important question, and our books have a lot to say about it. Here are the ways they describe.

- **Start by calming down.** The greatest miracle of multiplying bread and fish came after Jesus told the agitated crowd to sit down, and the counsel is to be careful for nothing but bring everything to God in prayer with thanksgiving, as Philippians 4:6 says [1]. A flustered person running from one emergency to another will not think clearly or hear from God, so give yourself time to calm down in His presence — sometimes it takes several days [1].

- **Be still and cut out the noise.** "Be still and know that I am God" (Psalm 46:10) is telling you to be silent and quiet so you can hear from God, because many Christians don't hear Him simply because they are too busy talking, chatting or singing [2]. One millionaire who got saved in prison explained that it was only there, with no one to talk to and no meetings to attend, that he began to commune with God [2].

- **Wait on God as a skill, and give it real time.** Waiting on God in a room for days on end is a skill few people have, and if you do not wait on Him you will not hear from Him — they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength (Isaiah 40:31) [4]. When the Levites were consecrated they had to stay at the tabernacle seven days, because you need that time to calm down in His presence [1].

- **Create an atmosphere where you can see and hear.** One pastor checked into a hotel to wait on God and found it terrible, because the only thing to see or hear was the television full of polluted stuff, and he could hardly pray in that cold, silent room [3]. He learned never to be anywhere without the ability to create an atmosphere for seeing and hearing from God, and he plays anointed preaching and music while he prays [3]. The sound of preaching creates the best atmosphere for spiritual things, and godly music creates a beautiful worship environment, so you can have your own little church service wherever you are [5].

- **Pray in tongues while you read.** Because praying in tongues leaves the mind unfruitful, as 1 Corinthians 14:14 says, you can read the Bible and ministry books while your spirit prays, which helps you pray for even longer hours [5].

- **Set yourself targets and time yourself.** Set a target of hours — ten, twenty, forty, fifty — and note the time when you begin and decide how long you will pray before you start [5][6]. Jesus prayed all night before choosing His disciples (Luke 6:12), and He was not impressed when Peter could not watch with Him one hour (Matthew 26:40) [5][6].

- **Wait together with others.** Jesus is present

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 8 of *Stir It Up*, chapter 12 of *What it means to be as Wise as a Serpent*, chapter 7 of *Seeing And Hearing*, chapter 9 of *The Privilege* and chapter 24 of *Church Growth*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 46:10; Isaiah 40:31; Daniel 1:4; Joel 2:15-17; Matthew 26:40; Luke 6:12; Acts 13:1-2; 1 Corinthians 14:14; Philippians 4:6.

items.question: Why is it dangerous to pretend to be strong when I'm actually struggling?
items.text:
It's a real danger, and the books speak to it plainly.

When you pretend to be strong, you cut yourself off from the help you need. If your pastor knows you are weak, he can pray for you, but if you pretend to be mighty, how can he know you need help [1][2]. Presenting yourself as strong when you are weak actually prevents your own deliverance — you are covering over the very thing that needs help [1][2].

The practical result is that no one comes to your aid. As a pastor, there are people he doesn't particularly need to visit because they seem strong, but when there is a weak one, he rushes there because that person needs attention [1][2]. When you look strong like Samson, you won't get any attention [1][2].

Samson is the picture of this: he was mighty in ministry, killing thousands, yet weak in his private life — mighty publicly but the opposite in private [1][2]. And there is a further danger in hiding it: a man of God who was a powerful preacher, moved many when he ministered, was also playing around with women in his church; when one of them asked how he could preach the next day after sinning with her, he answered that when he sinned like this the anointing came even more [2]. That is what pretending and covering can grow into.

The better way the books hold out is humility — talking about your weaknesses and personal problems rather than your achievements and victories, and confessing your sins more and more, as David did [7].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 2 of *Duality*, chapter 11 of *Spiritual Dangers* and chapter 17 of *Now We Are At War*.

Scriptures referenced: 2 Corinthians 12:9-10.

items.question: How do I deal with demonic attacks on my family?
items.book: Demons and How to Deal with Them
items.text:
I'm sorry your family is under this weight — that is a heavy thing to carry, and you are right to take it seriously.

The first thing the books would have you do is name what you are actually facing, because you cannot deal with what you have not identified. Jesus asked the madman of Gadara, "What is thy name?" (Luke 8:30), and the point is that specifically naming the problem is the key to dealing with demonic powers — so ask God to reveal the real identity of the spirits harassing your family [4].

Then look at what is happening among you. Unusual, illogical and persistent occurrences are demonic in nature; the madman of Gadara lived among the tombs and cut himself with stones, which no normal person does, and Job's attacks came one after another as a direct assault from Satan (Job 1:12) [5]. Where there is stealing, killing and destroying, you can be sure demons are on the loose, and those who do such things are walking in the image of Satan — so deal with the devil in your life by dealing properly with thieves, murderers and destroyers [1].

Watch too for conflict inside the family. Satan desires to draw you into battle with your husband, your wife, your child, your family; strife and quarrelling are demonic in their very nature, as James 3:14-15 says, and persistent conflict reveals the presence and activity of demonic creatures [2]. Do not let yourself be gathered into those fights [2].

And tighten your security, because you can defend yourself. Staying in the truth and avoiding deception tightens the security of your spirit against demons, since lies of any kind expose you to invasion (Ephesians 6:14) [7]. Practicing righteousness and avoiding sin does the same, for any sin can lead demons flying by to descend and invade (Ephesians 6:14) [7]. Emphasizing salvation tightens that security as well, and neglecting it exposes you [7].

One more thing worth naming: fear. Fear is an evil spirit, and its presence is the commonest sign of the presence of demons — it has power to change the whole course of your life if you allow it [8]. May the power of God set your household free from every evil spirit of fear [8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 8 and 18 of *One of You is a Devil*, chapters 4 and 20 of *Demons and How to Deal with Them* and chapters 5 and 24 of *Know Your Invisible Enemies*.

Scriptures referenced: Job 1:12; Mark 5:3; Mark 5:5; Luke 8:30; John 10:10; Ephesians 6:14; James 3:14-15; Revelation 16:13-14.

items.question: Why do people hear the same sermon differently?
items.text:
That's a question the books speak to directly, and they give several reasons why the same sermon lands so differently in different people.

- **What you see determines what you receive.** What you see will greatly determine what you will ultimately receive [1]. The eyes of the heart are trained on something invisible, spiritual and eternal, and that shapes what actually gets through [1].

- **People simply hear different things.** As you preach, one person hears your accent, another hears your grammar, another only remembers the stories or the jokes, while still others hear the principles and the Scriptures — and some hear the Spirit speaking, receiving wisdom and life-changing guidance from Him [1]. Jesus knew this, which is why He said, "Hearing they cannot hear" [1].

- **Some are dull of hearing and have closed their eyes.** The Scripture says their ears are dull of hearing and their eyes they have closed (Matthew 13:15) [1]. That dullness is a barrier the word cannot cross.

- **Lack of understanding blocks the message.** Many people have difficulty understanding issues, and that becomes a great barrier to receiving anything [1]. Understanding is crucial for the anointing to pass through the barrier of your mind and enter your spirit, and Scripture says, "with all thy getting get understanding" (Proverbs 4:7) [1].

- **The word must be mixed with faith.** Hebrews 4:1-2 says the gospel was preached to them too, but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it [8]. Judas sat at the table when Jesus said one of them would betray Him, and the message did not benefit him because he did not hear with faith [8].

- **Pride stops people from soaking in preaching.** Scripture says, "Hear ye and give ear! Be not proud!" — pride is the reason people stop listening to preaching [7]. When people are small in their own eyes they listen and soak it in; when they are big in their own eyes they say, "It's all the same thing," and hear nothing [7].

- **Every message is unique, even when titles are similar.** You may hear a casual side comment that changes your whole life [7]. One man listened to eighty-five messages on a single topic by a preacher he admired, over and over, and noticed an upgrade in the anointing on his life as the weeks passed [7].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 12 of *Steps to the Anointing* and chapters 10 and 16 of *Seeing And Hearing*.

Scriptures referenced: Proverbs 4:7; Matthew 13:14-15; Luke 22:22-23; 2 Timothy 2:1-2; Hebrews 4:1-2.

items.question: How can I recognize when someone is using flattery or food to lead me into sin?
items.text:
The passages speak directly to flattery, and they also speak to how sin spreads through close company. Here is what our books say.

- **Watch for excessive, insincere praise.** Flattery is excessively praising someone insincerely in order to gain favor for yourself, and people who flatter you cannot be trusted [2][1]. Be on guard every time you meet someone who effusively praises you and your ministry, because flattery is a sign of disloyalty and of someone who will eventually leave you [1].

- **Notice when the praise makes you out to be more than you are.** Flattery makes you think you are what you are not; it is an injection of pride, and pride goes before a fall [2]. In Ghana, official flatterers at traditional gatherings hail the chiefs with accolades so fantastic they make the chiefs feel like God himself — "you are the one who leans on a rock and makes it break," "you are the one who kills the lion with your bare hands" — and no man is a god, for all men are mortal [2].

- **Test the flatterer's words against Scripture.** The Bible warns that there is no faithfulness in the mouth of flatterers, whose throat is an open sepulchre (Psalms 5:9), and that a flattering mouth works ruin (Proverbs 26:28) [1][2]. A flatterer's praises are a mask for his true intentions [1].

- **Watch how they treat others' honor.** A journalist once told Bishop Dag Heward-Mills he should be president of Ghana because of his achievements; when asked why he had not suggested his own pastor, who had achieved more, the man dismissed his pastor as old stock and no longer relevant — the hallmarks of a dangerous flatterer [1].

- **Beware of close company with those who live in sin.** Sin is a mystery that spreads like leaven through dough: liars make you into liars, fornicators make others fornicators, and fellowshiping deeply with the wrong people passes their lifestyle on to you, which is why Paul said not to keep company with a brother who is a fornicator, covetous, an idolater, a railer, a drunkard, or an extortioner (1 Corinthians 5:11) [6].

- **Do not be impressed because you are simple-minded.** It is the simple-minded who are impressed by the flattery of wicked men [1].

Our books have not directly addressed food being used to lead someone into sin.

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 9 of *Those who leave you*, chapter 3 of *Poison: Taming The Tongue* and chapter 1 of *BEMA Judgment And Justice*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 5:9; Proverbs 26:28; Zechariah 1:5; 1 Corinthians 5:1-7; 1 Corinthians 5:11; 1 Thessalonians 2:5; 2 Thessalonians 2:7; Jude 16.

items.question: Why is my church not growing?
items.book: Why Is This Church Not Working?
items.text:
I'm sorry you're carrying this weight — it's a hard question to sit with, and I'm glad you asked it plainly.

The books point to several possible reasons, and they don't all say the same thing, so let me lay them out for you.

**It may be warfare.** Something is fighting you; that is why your church is not growing. Satan is the god of this world who has captured the hearts and minds of billions of souls, and he will not give up any one without a fight — he only gives them up through a real war. Pastors who are not prepared to go to war cannot have church growth, so you must have a warfare attitude and a warfare mind, not a peaceful "peace time" disposition [1]. The gates of hell are postured against the church, and demons keep coming out of those gates to attack the advancing church, so you must fight to achieve church growth [6].

**It may be a low capacity for studying.** You need to study to show yourself a pastor who is not ashamed of the size of his congregation, as 2 Timothy 2:15 says. It is more difficult to be a successful pastor than to be a medical doctor, and people who do not study books on ministry and church growth will not have growth. Church growth is a complex thing that takes great understanding, and a failing church that is not growing is a revelation of a lack of knowledge, wisdom and understanding [2].

**It may be a lack of diligence.** Diligence speaks of the constant effort to accomplish, and the reason you have not risen in ministry is passivity — not participating readily, actively, or emotionally when expected to. Because you do not participate readily and actively in your ministry work, you constantly need supervision, and once you need constant supervision, you will not excel. Pastors who are diligent and make a constant effort to accomplish something are the only ones who have working churches [3].

**It may be the location.** You are not supposed to set up your tent to worship the Lord in just any location; it must be the right place which God has chosen, as Deuteronomy 12:13-14 says. One church was planted in the north of a city and did not work; when it was moved to the south, it began to work and grew into a mega church. Perhaps your church is in a dangerous location, or too far for people to come, or in a neighbourhood racially hostile to the people you invite — it may be time to relocate so that many more people can come [4].

**It may be the wrong growth strategy.** A house is built through wisdom, and by a series of steps, as Proverbs 24:3-4 says; the wisdom that achieves great things with a series of steps is called strategy. No great achievement involves just one step, and church growth will by all means involve a series of steps, manoeuvres or stratagems. Many pastors are not

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 3 of *The Double Mega Missionary Church*, chapters 11, 12 and 18 of *Why Is This Church Not Working?* and chapter 11 of *Attempt Great Things for God*.

Scriptures referenced: Deuteronomy 12:13-14; Proverbs 22:29; Jeremiah 30:19; Mark 6:2; Acts 16:5; 2 Timothy 2:15.

items.question: What diseases can you get from having sex before marriage?
items.text:
Yes, this is a sober subject, and our books speak plainly about it. Fornication is sexual intercourse before marriage [3][6], and the books warn that it opens the door to real physical harm.

- **Sexually transmitted diseases.** The germs that cause these diseases gain access into you when you commit fornication, and the books list ten of them: Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, Non-Specific Urethritis, liver diseases from Hepatitis B, Herpes Genitalis, Vaginitis, Lymphogranuloma venereum, Soft Sore (Chancroid), urinary tract infection, and cancer of the cervix, which frequent sex at an early age predisposes you to [1][2].
- **HIV and AIDS.** Fornication will kill you if you acquire the Human Immuno Virus, and unless God works a miracle you may die of AIDS [1][2]. HIV is described as a death sentence, and the books note sadly that there are many Christians in charismatic churches who are HIV positive — a laboratory technician told of a blood donation event in a charismatic church where, out of about a hundred donors, a large percentage tested positive [2].
- **Danger even to a faithful partner.** A faithful partner can develop a sexually transmitted disease through no fault of theirs when the other partner has sex outside the marriage, and so a life-threatening problem is introduced into the marriage [4].
- **The protection of waiting.** If you wait till you marry before having sex, you may save yourself from all these diseases [1][2]. When marriage comes before sex, these things ideally do not occur, because sex is supposed to be experienced only after marriage [5][7].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 3 of *Spiritual Dangers*, chapters 2 and 3 of *All About Fornication*, chapter 11 of *The Beauty The Beast and The Pastor*, chapter 14 of *The Words of Jesus* and chapter 8 of *The Top Ten Mistakes that Pastors Make*.

Scriptures referenced: Jeremiah 3:15; Ephesians 5:3.

items.question: What mistakes do pastors usually make that hurt their ministry?
items.book: The Top Ten Mistakes that Pastors Make
items.text:
Here are the mistakes the books warn about most often.

- **Choosing to bear little fruit.** A pastor can leave a fruitful place for somewhere with no one to preach to, or stay where he has only forty members when he could have had a thousand, because what he really wants is a European address or an American green card rather than fruit [1]. Some also refuse to bear much fruit under someone else's banner, since being independent matters more to them than being fruitful [1]. God is glorified when we bear much fruit, as John 15:8 says [1].

- **Turning into a Pharisee.** After years in ministry it becomes easy to care about the uppermost rooms and chief seats, the very thing Jesus rebuked in Matthew 23:6-7 [2]. It is always a mistake not to concentrate on the one or two instructions that would genuinely please the one over you [3].

items.question: How can I know if I'm on the wrong path in life?
items.text:
Here are the ways our books say you can tell.

- **Watch for symptoms and signs.** A symptom is an outward clue to something hidden, and if it is detected early it can save a life; a doctor reads a shaking hand as a sign of liver trouble, while a layman sees only a spasm [7]. The same is true spiritually — you look for the signs so you can know [7].

- **Check whether your heart is condemning you.** God has given everyone a conscience, that quiet inner voice that checks us when we go wrong, and your heart has the ability to condemn you for wrongdoing [4]. It is only when your heart is not condemning you that you have confidence toward God, as 1 John 3:20-21 says [4]. If you keep ignoring that voice it becomes deadened and hardened — what Paul called a conscience seared with a hot iron [4].

- **Count the company you are keeping.** The way to tell whether you are on the broad way or the narrow way is by the number of people on it: the broad way has many, the narrow way few [3]. In this world the road with a lot of people on it is seen as the right road, but not so with Christ — He warned that you must be among the few who choose Him [3].

- **Ask whether you are following someone who knows the way.** There are people who have not been to Heaven and yet boldly declare they do not know where they are going; do not follow such people [6]. Jesus Christ knows the way to Heaven because He has been there before, and He said, "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me" (John 14:6) [6].

- **Test the way against the ways that seem right.** There is a way which seems right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death (Proverbs 14:12) [8]. The way of heaping up riches is not the way to God (Ecclesiastes 4:8), and neither is a way of pleasure [8].

- **Let the fear of judgment keep you steady.** We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, and knowing the terror of the Lord we persuade men (2 Corinthians 5:10-11) [5]. Those who have no fear of judgment live anyhow and stray from the path of righteousness, while a proper fear of God's judgment keeps you steadfast and unmoveable from the path of life [5].

- **Be led by the Spirit rather than by other powers.** As Christians we do not need to consult satanic powers to know the future; God has graciously given us the Holy Spirit to guide us, and being led by the Spirit of God is a sign that you are a true Christian (Romans 8:14) [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 7 and 24 of *The Art of Hearing*, chapters 28, 50 and 65 of *How You Can Preach Salvation*, chapter 3 of *How you can become a strong Christian* and chapter 5 of *Backsliding*.

items.question: What does it mean to build a church on a deep foundation?
items.text:
Building a church on a deep foundation means going deeper before you go higher — the deeper and stronger the foundation, the greater and taller the building can be [1]. Jesus told the story of two men who each built a house: the wise one dug deep and laid his foundation on rock, so when the flood beat against it the house could not be shaken, while the foolish one built on the ground without a foundation and it fell at once, and great was its ruin (Luke 6:47-49) [1]. So the depth is not about the size of the crowd but about what the whole structure rests on.

That foundation is made of specific things you must not set aside: salvation through the blood and cross of Jesus Christ, faithfulness and loyalty, evangelism and outreach, teaching and sticking to the word of God, tithes and offerings as the financing of God's work, and the truth that God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have eternal life [1]. These are the first principles of the oracles of God, and when they come under attack you defend them by teaching those first principles again, as Hebrews 5:12 says [2].

It also means the foundation is the most important part of the building, which makes your earliest members the most important members the church will ever have — Jesus always had a special place and reward for the apostles because they were His foundational members, as Ephesians 2:20 says [6][8]. So you don't rebuke or shout at those few; you preach faith, hope, stabilization and a better tomorrow, and you are bold and shameless in your preaching, because the shamelessly persistent person gets results (Luke 11:8) [6][8].

And a deep foundation is a hard one. You cannot build a big church on a soft leader; the church is the house of God and needs a rock as its foundation, because the rain will descend, the floods will come and the winds will blow on what you are building (Matthew 7:24-25) [3]. Jesus renamed Peter "the rock" because He knew a hard person was needed to build the worldwide church (Matthew 16:18), and He commended John the Baptist for not being a reed shaken by the wind [3]. Being on the rock does not exempt you, either — the same bad wind that blows on the person doing wrong blows on the good person's house [4].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 6 of *Going Deeper and Doing More*, chapters 30 and 41 of *Church Growth*, chapter 20 of *Church Planting* and chapter 7 of *The Mega Church*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 11:3; Matthew 7:24-27; Matthew 16:18; Luke 6:47-49; Luke 11:8; Ephesians 2:20; Hebrews 5:12.

items.question: What does it mean when someone constantly accuses others and tries to control them?
items.text:
When someone constantly accuses others and works to control them, the books describe this as something more than a personality flaw — it is a spiritual dynamic with a name.

Accusations are one of Satan's chief weapons, and one of their purposes is control: through persistent accusations, a person can stop you from doing things they dislike and steer your decisions onto a course different from what God intended [1]. The book calls this witchcraft, defining it as the use of any power other than God's power to control people — and it notes that this kind of control is hard to recognize, sometimes even by the one doing it [1]. A person with a controlling spirit is described as a witch, wielding power through relentless accusations [2].

The accuser's motives are often hidden, and the book lists several aims behind them. Accusations degrade the accused in their own eyes, so they lose the zeal to do good [4]. They generate hatred and bitterness in the one accused, opening a door for further harm [3]. And they bring separation — a pastor and his assistant, or a husband and wife, grow distant as accusations pile up over the years [3].

Accusations are also described as a manifestation of hatred: "your accuser is the one who hates you most" [2]. And fear plays a part too — people who constantly expect the worst may accuse those closest to them, suspecting a spouse of an affair or an honest worker of stealing, because their own fears are being voiced as accusations [2].

One example the book gives is a minister who no longer felt free in his own home: his wife would search his phone for incriminating messages and evidence of questionable calls, and witchcraft had modified his domestic behaviour [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 3 and 4 of *Those Who Accuse You*.

Scriptures referenced: Matthew 25:24-25; John 15:25.

items.question: What are creeping things in the spiritual sense and how do I pray against them in my church?
items.text:
Creeping things are the things that sneak up on a church without anyone realizing it — great changes that take place slowly over a long time, so that most people hardly notice them happening [1]. The book names four that creep upon all churches: deception, wrong attitudes like laziness, complacency and unbelief, familiarity, and the shifting of priorities — for example, a church becoming a health and educational organisation instead of a missionary society [1].

The clearest picture given is deception: the church in Europe did not become godless overnight; the spirit of deception crept on it slowly [1]. Familiarity is called one of the most dangerous of these creepers — without realising it, a church stops holding its pastor in esteem, even while claiming that it does [1]. The sign the author noticed in his own ministry was that the response he received outside his own church was higher than at home, with more miracles and greater receptivity [1].

As for praying against them, the counsel is that intercessory prayer is necessary to keep out these spiritual creepers, and that it will fight the creeping familiarity that kills the flow of the Spirit [1]. Beyond that, the books speak of binding the works of darkness in prayer — forbidding demonic powers from manoeuvring and roaming around you, and preventing them from being comfortable around your dwelling place [3]. They also tell of a pastor who found a creature living in the ceiling of his church building, rebuked it and commanded it out; a year later the confusion, complaining and quarrelling were gone and the church grew considerably [4]. The lesson drawn is that persistent opposition, frustration and a slowing down of your vision are signs of demon powers released specifically against you, and that you should rise up and expose and arrest the activities of opposition spirits [4].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 21 of *Transform Your Pastoral Ministry*, chapter 7 of *Everything By Prayer 

Nothing Without Prayer* and chapter 9 of *One of You is a Devil*.

Scriptures referenced: Genesis 1:25-26; Daniel 7:25.

items.question: What does the Bible say about being a shepherd like Jesus?
items.text:
Being a shepherd is not merely a job—it is a privilege, because you are joining Jesus Christ Himself in His chosen profession. He called Himself the Good Shepherd, and when you accept the work of shepherding, you are accepting an honour, not just a role [1].

- **You are joining Jesus in His own work.** Jesus Christ was a shepherd, and He called Himself the Good Shepherd; to shepherd is to take up the very job He did on earth [1]. The word "shepherd" in John 10:11 is the Greek word *poimen*, the same word translated "pastor" in Ephesians 4:11, so what the Lord was really saying was, "I am the good pastor" [6][7].

- **You are a caring, loving guide.** A shepherd is someone God has called to look after sheep—a caring, loving guide—and God sees His people as sheep who need love, care and guidance, not as a random collection of animals [5]. The work involves visiting people, praying for them, counselling with the word of God, and preaching and teaching [1].

- **You lead by going first.** A good shepherd leads his sheep; that means being practically available for them to see and learn from you in every area of life and ministry [2][7]. Anything you want your sheep to do, you must first do it yourself—if you want your members to pray, you must practically lead them into prayer, because when the sheep see the shepherd taking the lead, they are convinced the ground is safe [2][7].

- **You feed the sheep.** The best food for sheep is the green pasture, and Jesus said to Peter, "If you love me, feed my sheep" (John 21:16) [1]. The principal duty of a shepherd is to feed the flock, so a person who wants to be a pastor must develop the ability to preach and teach [8].

- **You help people prosper.** "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1) means I shall not be in difficulty, I shall not be poor, and I shall not lack any good thing—so a shepherd is privileged to help people prosper [1].

- **You go after the lost.** According to Jesus, to be a good shepherd you must leave the ninety-nine and go looking for the one lost sheep (Luke 15:4-7) [4]. A good shepherd seeks to save sinners, which are lost, and if you are not interested in souls, it is worth questioning whether you have a genuine call to be a shepherd [8].

- **You do it with all your might.** Scripture says, "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might" (Ecclesiastes 9:10)—so if you are going to be a pastor, be a good one [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 2 of *The Privilege*, chapters 1, 7, 9 and 13 of *What It Means to Become a Shepherd*, chapter 2 of *How You Can Preach Salvation* and chapter 8 of *Church Growth*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 23:1-6; Psalms 95:6-7; Ecclesiastes 9:10; Matthew 9:36; Matthew 18:12; Luke 15:4-32; Luke 19:10; John 6:35; John 8:23; John 8:58 and 17 more.

items.question: How does the grace of God help my ministry reach more people and get support?
items.book: How You Can Make Full proof of Your Ministry
items.text:
Grace is God's undeserved help and favour surrounding the gift He has placed in you, and it is grace that decides how far your ministry reaches and how many people it touches [1]. Here is how the books describe it at work.

- **Grace sets the reach of your ministry.** The grace of God is why some pastors have larger churches and others smaller, why some evangelists draw larger crowds and others fewer, and why some see outstanding miracles and others only minor ones [1]. You fulfil your ministry not only by God's call and purpose but by flowing in the grace available to you [1].

- **Grace carries your gift to many people.** Just as the grace of God that brings salvation appeared to all men (Titus 2:11-12), it is that same grace that brings your gift to many people — which is why some have much patronage, many readers, many attenders and many supporters [1].

- **Grace draws support and provision.** In the early church, great grace was upon them all, and no one among them lacked, for those who owned lands or houses sold them and laid the proceeds at the apostles' feet (Acts 4:33-35) [1]. That great grace showed itself as unity and financial provision, and the disciples fulfilled their ministry according to the support and unity they enjoyed [1].

- **Grace makes you attractive and draws people to listen.** Charisma means manifestation of grace, and a charismatic person receives multiple manifestations of gracefulness and beauty that give him a magnetic appeal [8]. It is not your looks, dressing, education or height that draws people, but the influence of the Holy Spirit, and it is the Holy Spirit who causes people to be drawn to help and support such a person [8].

- **Grace lifts the lay person to minister beyond his station.** When lay people grow a church as though they were full-time priests, it is because of the grace of God, which helps a layman minister as though he were a prophet, apostle, evangelist, teacher or pastor [4]. When grace is at work, a person is supernaturally lifted up [4].

- **Be strong in the grace you can identify.** Paul told Timothy to be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 2:1), meaning he should emphasise and major in the things where he recognised grace at work [2]. When the disciples saw that Antioch was experiencing the grace of God, they moved there and emphasised the ministry in that city rather than holding on to Jerusalem [2]. Open your eyes to see what God has given you and what works for you, and walk in that favour [2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 17 of *How You Can Make Full proof of Your Ministry*, chapter 18 of *Laikos Lay People and the Ministry* and chapter 16 of *The Sweet Influences of the Anointing*.

Scriptures referenced: Acts 4:33-35; Acts 11:19-24; Galatians 2:14; Galatians 2:18; Galatians 2:21; 2 Timothy 1:8-9; 2 Timothy 2:1; Titus 2:11-12.

It is not your looks, dressing, education or height that draws people, but the influence of the Holy Spirit, and it is the Holy Spirit who causes people to be drawn to help and support such a person.

- **Grace lifts the lay person to minister beyond his station.** When lay people grow a church as though they were full-time priests, it is because of the grace of God, which helps a layman minister as though he were a prophet, apostle, evangelist, teacher or pastor.
When grace is at work, a person is supernaturally lifted up.

- **Be strong in the grace you can identify.** Paul told Timothy to be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 2:1), meaning he should emphasise and major in the things where he recognised grace at work.
When the disciples saw that Antioch was experiencing the grace of God, they moved there and emphasised the ministry in that city rather than holding on to Jerusalem.
Open your eyes to see what God has given you and what works for you, and walk in that favour.

items.question: What does God want from a church that has already been through a lot?
items.book:
Can’t You Do
Just a Little Bit More?
items.text:
That's a heavy question, and I want to answer it gently, because a church that has "been through a lot" is carrying real scars.

God's will for His church is that His house may be filled — Jesus told the story of a master who sent his servant out to the highways and hedges to compel people to come in, "that my house may be filled" (Luke 14:23), and the master was not content with just a few guests at his party [2]. That same will reaches out to the whole world, since we are sent to preach the gospel to every creature (Mark 16:15-16), which means the harvest of souls is meant to be very large [2]. So a church that has suffered is not excused from fruitfulness; bearing much fruit is how the Father is glorified, as John 15:8 says, and fruitfulness must stay on top of the agenda of every true man of God [7].

But do not read your suffering as God's rejection. Suffering is actually a sign that you are a good Christian — Paul said he laboured and suffered reproach because he trusted in the living God (1 Timothy 4:10), and "all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution" (2 Timothy 3:12) [1]. You must give up the notion that suffering means defeat or failure, or that God is angry with you; those thoughts only weaken you [1]. Christianity is a religion that does not only involve believing but also suffering — we are appointed unto it (Philippians 1:29, 1 Thessalonians 3:3) [6]. At a pastor's funeral, after years of slow and painful decline, his widow told the crowd that his death was not a defeat, and that our theology must include suffering [6].

And know that some suffering belongs specifically to your calling. A minister once told Bishop Dag Heward-Mills that he had never been through such trials in building his church — but it turned out he had never founded a church at all; he had been made senior pastor of one already in existence, and the suffering of founding a church is different from the suffering of growing one [4]. Some people face challenges in their marriages just because of their calling, and they should not be despised for it [4].

So keep fighting. Make up your mind to fight till the end of your life, in every situation, and don't give up — God is allowing you to encounter the sufferings and experiences that His generals and chosen ones go through [1].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 5 of *Losing, Suffering, Sacrificing and Dying*, chapter 1 of *The Mega Church* and chapter 4 of *The Words of Jesus*.

Scriptures referenced: Mark 16:15-16; Luke 14:1-35; John 15:8; Acts 9:15-16; Philippians 1:29; 1 Thessalonians 3:3; 1 Timothy 4:10; 2 Timothy 3:12.

items.question: What happens spiritually to a Christian who commits fornication?
items.text:
This is a heavy thing to carry, and I'm glad you're asking it honestly. Here is what our books say happens spiritually.

**Your soul is damaged.** The Bible says that whoever commits adultery lacks understanding and destroys his own soul (Proverbs 6:32), and that means fornication has a real effect on you spiritually — you may not know exactly how, but it does affect you and leads you to backslide [1][2]. With experience it has been seen that when someone commits fornication, his spiritual life takes a nosedive and his lifestyle changes; the destruction of the soul has begun [1][2].

**You make covenants.** Sex is meant to be a binding experience, and when blood is shed a covenant is created, so sleeping with different people may actually be entering into union with them [1][7]. Paul asked, "shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid" (1 Corinthians 6:15) [1][7]. Such covenants are for real and can affect you for the rest of your life; some Christians have been crippled all their Christian lives because of fornication and never rise out of that covenant [1][7].

**Evil spirits come in.** Fornication brings evil spirits into your life — Revelation 18:2 speaks of Babylon becoming the habitation of devils and the hold of every foul spirit [7].

**Your conscience hardens.** As you continue to sin without repenting, your conscience becomes hardened the way the palm of your hand grows callous with hard work, and when it is gone, that element within you that could stop you from going far from God is gone too [8]. You stop being touched by the anointing, the Word, the preaching, or the Holy Ghost, and you can commit wilder and wilder sins [8].

**You can be spiritual and still carnal.** Samson is the picture of this: the Spirit of the Lord moved him at times (Judges 13:25), he was the spiritual leader of Israel for twenty years, and yet he had a woman problem and went out for prostitutes one after another [5]. There are preachers who are mighty in ministry and weak in private life, and some who say they preach best after fornicating — the difference between them and you is only a gradual process of hardening [5][8].

One more thing the books say plainly: it pays to obey God, but it is very expensive to disobey Him [1][2].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 3 of *Spiritual Dangers*, chapter 3 of *All About Fornication*, chapter 2 of *Duality* and chapter 5 of *How you can become a strong Christian*.

Scriptures referenced: Judges 13:25; 1 Samuel 15:22; Proverbs 6:32; 1 Corinthians 6:15; 1 Corinthians 6:18-19; Jude 19; Revelation 18:2.

items.question: What is the secret to answered prayer?
items.text:
The books speak of this often, and they give several keys rather than one secret. Here is what they say.

- **Learn to pray for yourself.** God wants you to be able to come to your heavenly Father directly, not to depend only on your pastor or on prayer warriors; their prayers are a bonus, not your foundation, and you are righteous enough in Christ to get results yourself [5].

- **Let the Word of God abide in you.** God does not act outside His Word, and His Word directs you in prayer; He does not answer foolish prayers or do things against His Word, so stay in the Word if you want answers [1][2].

- **Obey the Lord's commandments.** God answers the prayers of people who obey Him, and a life of disobedience closes that door; as 1 John 3:22 says, we receive what we ask because we keep His commandments and do what pleases Him [1][2].

- **Be a fruit-bearing Christian.** God has linked answered prayer to bearing fruit; as John 15:16 says, we are chosen and ordained to bring forth fruit that remains, so that whatever we ask the Father in Jesus' name He may give us [2].

- **Stay in fellowship.** If you are walking in the light you will have fellowship with others who are in the light, as 1 John 1:7 says; staying in fellowship is an important key to receiving the Lord's blessings [2].

- **Persist in prayer.** Jesus taught that we should always pray and not faint, and He told of a man who got bread from a friend at midnight only because of his persistence, and of a widow who wore down an unjust judge by her continual coming; praying over and over with determination is one valid expression of faith [3][8].

- **Pray in faith, even once.** Praying once is also an expression of faith, and both persistence and faith are valid, both were taught by Jesus, and both bring results [3].

- **Come to God with praise and thanksgiving.** Praise and worship bring the presence of God, and Scripture says to enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise, and to come before His presence with singing [7].

And underneath all of it, the books insist that God really does answer: He says, "He shall call upon me, and I will answer him" (Psalm 91:15), and Jesus said, "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you" (Luke 11:9) [5].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 3 and 4 of *100% Answered Prayer*, chapter 9 of *How to Pray* and chapter 12 of *The Anointing and the Presence*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 91:15; Psalms 100:1-2; Psalms 100:4; Psalms 119:133; Isaiah 58:9; Luke 11:5-9; John 15:16; 2 Corinthians 5:21; James 5:16; 1 John 1:7 and 1 more.

items.question: How do I get my life ready to die?
items.text:
It's a good and serious thing to ask, and our books speak to it plainly.

- **Set your house in order.** To prepare is to set your house in order — to get ready for death and eternity, making arrangements for the end of your life here and the beginning of eternity [1]. Hezekiah was told to do this very thing, and the command is given to all of us, not to him alone [1].

- **Be ready at any moment, not just in a later season.** To prepare is to enter into a constant state of readiness, because God may need you today and not next year [3]. Scripture says to be instant in season and out of season (2 Timothy 4:2), and being ready in season and out of season means being ready all the time [3]. It is not safe to assume there is more time; since we don't know the day or the hour, we must be ready all the time [6].

- **Come to God through Christ.** You can only be ready through the blood of Jesus who died for you [7]. You prepare to meet your God by giving your life to Christ and being washed in the blood of Jesus [8].

- **Live as a strong Christian, so you die the death of the righteous.** If you live the life of a strong Christian you will end well and die the death of a righteous man [2]. You can choose to be steadfast, faithful, unmovable, spiritual, fruitful and mature [2].

- **Fulfil your ministry.** The only way to die the death of a righteous person is to fulfil your ministry; when you have done all that God wants you to do, you will go out of this world in peace saying, "It is finished!" [2]. Paul could say he had run his race, finished his ministry and fulfilled his call, and so was ready to meet his God [4].

- **Prepare for the gospel and preach it.** One of the ways to get yourself ready for eternity is to prepare for the gospel and preach the gospel for the rest of your life [1]. What you did with the gospel of Jesus Christ, and whether you served the Lord, will matter so much in eternity [1].

- **Make a plan for death, as a good general does.** A good general knows he can die and prepares for the reality of death; if you ignore that death can happen, you open yourself up to a very deep crisis [5]. One soldier showed the chain he wore around his neck, inscribed with his name and number, given so his body could be identified if he died in battle — all the soldiers had to wear it [5].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 11 and 12 of *The Preparation of the Gospel*, chapter 10 of *How you can become a strong Christian*, chapter 47 of *A Good General*, chapter 4 of *Backsliding* and chapter 37 of *How You Can Preach Salvation*.

Scriptures referenced: Numbers 23:10; 1 Samuel 20:3; 2 Kings 20:1-7; Daniel 12:3; Amos 4:12; Malachi 3:18; Luke 12:1-59; Romans 1:15-16; 1 Thessalonians 4:16-18; 2 Timothy 4:2 and 1 more.

items.question: How do I get closer to God through apostles, prophets, pastors, teachers and evangelists?
items.text:
The books speak to this directly, and they treat these five gifts as doors God has given you.

- **Receive them as doors, not obstacles.** People do not become close to God until they accept apostles, prophets, pastors, teachers and evangelists; they are doors for you, and those too stiff to go through them will never experience a certain level of God's presence [1]. You cannot go far without true apostles and prophets, and you will not get far without a pastor, a teacher or an evangelist [1].

- **Let them be personal to you.** The writer says he became closer to God by accepting great prophets like Kenneth Hagin and great pastors like Yonggi Cho into his life — they were doors for him [1]. Through such people, you can get closer to God [1].

- **Don't be driven away by suspicion.** Some will say, "Do not trust a man," or "Be careful of these money-grabbing men of God"; what is actually happening is that you are being driven away from the five-pillared door to the presence of God [1]. It is time to receive your apostle, prophet and pastor so that you can be near to God [1].

- **Be thankful for them.** Be thankful to God's servants who are sent to you, as 1 Thessalonians 5:12 says — appreciate those who diligently labor among you and give you instruction [4]. God's servants are God's gift to you; when God wants to be kind to you, He sends you a man of God, and these men are an expression of His love to you [4].

- **Test what you receive by the Word.** Under the New Testament, the declarations of prophets are to be judged or assessed, and the Word of God provides the standard by which we assess what is happening, as 1 Corinthians 14:29 shows [3]. A true prophet will be known by his fruits: if the end result of his ministry is destabilization and members being moved to and fro, that is not the New Testament prophet's work, for prophets are meant to keep the saints from being tossed to and fro, as Ephesians 4:11,14 says [3].

- **Look for the Word in their ministry.** A minister in the office of a prophet will primarily function in preaching and teaching, so beware of so-called prophets who do not preach the Word of God but only give personal prophecies [6][8]. Anything that does not put the Word of God in its proper place is doomed to failure with the passage of time [6][8].

- **Draw near to God yourself, daily.** The only way to know Him personally is a regular daily quiet time, because it is up to you to draw near to Him, as James 4:8 says — draw nigh to God, and He will draw nigh to you [7]. There is no point running around on His behalf

Scriptures referenced: Matthew 16:15-17; Matthew 16:21-23; Luke 7:16; 1 Corinthians 14:29; Ephesians 4:11-14; 1 Thessalonians 5:12; James 4:8.

items.question: How can I stay focused and really connect with God when I pray instead of getting distracted or falling asleep?
items.text:
It's a real struggle, and you're not alone in it — the disciples themselves couldn't stay awake with Jesus for even one hour. Here are some ways the books point to:

- **Create an atmosphere where you can see and hear from God.** One of our authors checked into a silent hotel room to wait on God and found he could hardly pray in that cold, hard, silent place, so he resolved never to be anywhere without the ability to create an atmosphere of seeing and hearing — playing anointed preaching and music while he prays, so that prayer becomes like being part of a miracle service [1].

- **Disconnect your phone.** The telephone is a favourite tool the devil uses to interrupt prayer, and the lingering feeling that you might miss an important call keeps you from switching it off; needless interruptions break a precious hour of prayer into piecemeal five-minute sessions, so decide that if you are serious about praying, you must disconnect it — the world can wait [2].

- **Issue a "do not disturb" notice.** Since you don't live on an island, you need the cooperation of those you live with; just as they wouldn't disturb you in the bathroom, they must not disturb you in prayer, so don't be ashamed to let friends and family know when you are praying [2].

- **Gain control of your sleep by going to bed early.** Watching involves staying up at night to pray, and if you learn to stay awake at night you will pray far more hours than those who only fast and pray; learn to overcome sleep by going to bed early so you can rise a great while before day, which was the life of Jesus — as Mark 1:35 says, He rose up a great while before day and went to a solitary place to pray [3].

- **Pray alone, not only in a group.** Many Christians can only pray in a crowd and cannot stay in a room alone for one hour, which is a great handicap; if you can pray three hours on your own, you can pray six with others, and every time you expand your ability to pray alone you expand your ability to achieve great things in prayer [4].

- **Make prayer a fixed part of your life, even when you're busy.** When our author was a busy medical student with no time to pray, he prayed late at night and was so sleepy he had to walk about to stay awake — one night he actually fell asleep while walking and only woke when he walked into the Spanish Department building; God saw his earnest desire to keep praying despite an impossible schedule [7].

- **Pray at set times and all the time.** Praying in the afternoon shows that in the heat of the day and the thick of the battle you recognize God as the most important force in your life — a little time off your lunch break will do you more good than a plate of rice [5][8]. Pray in the evenings too, staying awake rather than

Scriptures referenced: Matthew 26:36-40; Matthew 26:42-44; Mark 1:35; Mark 6:46; Luke 6:12-13; 1 Thessalonians 5:17.

- **Issue a "do not disturb" notice.** Since you don't live on an island, you need the cooperation of those you live with; just as they wouldn't disturb you in the bathroom, they must not disturb you in prayer, so don't be ashamed to let friends and family know when you are praying.

- **Gain control of your sleep by going to bed early.** Watching involves staying up at night to pray, and if you learn to stay awake at night you will pray far more hours than those who only fast and pray; learn to overcome sleep by going to bed early so you can rise a great while before day, which was the life of Jesus — as Mark 1:35 says, He rose up a great while before day and went to a solitary place to pray.

- **Pray alone, not only in a group.** Many Christians can only pray in a crowd and cannot stay in a room alone for one hour, which is a great handicap; if you can pray three hours on your own, you can pray six with others, and every time you expand your ability to pray alone you expand your ability to achieve great things in prayer.

- **Make prayer a fixed part of your life, even when you're busy.** When our author was a busy medical student with no time to pray, he prayed late at night and was so sleepy he had to walk about to stay awake — one night he actually fell asleep while walking and only woke when he walked into the Spanish Department building; God saw his earnest desire to keep praying despite an impossible schedule.

- **Pray at set times and all the time.** Praying in the afternoon shows that in the heat of the day and the thick of the battle you recognize God as the most important force in your life — a little time off your lunch break will do you more good than a plate of rice.

items.question: How can a husband help his wife stay beautiful?
items.text:
A husband has a real part to play in his wife's beauty, and the books speak to it warmly.

- **Invest in the factors beauty depends on.** Beauty depends on many things — hair, dressing, make-up, even the time of day — so a wise husband invests in those factors and does whatever he has to do to make his wife look even more beautiful, remembering that you reap what you sow [2].
- **Tell her what you like.** A husband should tell his wife how he likes her hair and how he wants it done, and say plainly when a style doesn't suit her, since she is looking beautiful for him [2].
- **Be concerned about her dressing.** A good husband takes an interest in which dress his wife wears, because her beauty also depends on her dressing, and he should encourage her to make every attempt to dress nicely [2].
- **Nourish and cherish her.** A man is to love his wife as his own body, nourishing and cherishing her with the Word of God and with physical things, as Ephesians 5:25-29 says, and it is for his own good to beautify his wife [3].
- **Make her feel loved, wanted and accepted.** Let her feel accepted and special, stay at home as often as possible and give her companionship, don't be harsh with her, and listen to her a lot and encourage her to talk [3].
- **Speak lovingly, never scornfully.** A husband must not make scathing remarks about his wife's body, but should speak the truth in love, as Ephesians 4:15 says, and love her as his own body, as Ephesians 5:28 says [6].
- **Be a devoted husband.** A devoted husband says wonderful things about his wife, respects her and treats her with great dignity, is loving and caring, treats her as a partner, buys her gifts, takes her out, and always appears in public with her [8].

And a word for her too, since it is part of the same picture: a wife should take time to do her hair and not stop investing in her personal beauty, and let her husband always see her beautiful hair [1].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 11, 32 and 40 of *Model Marriage*, chapter 7 of *Beauty* and chapter 12 of *The Beauty The Beast and The Pastor*.

items.question: What does the Bible say about wasting opportunities?
items.text:
The books speak plainly about this, and they return again and again to one story — the prodigal son, who took his share of his father's goods, journeyed to a far country, and wasted it all in riotous living (Luke 15:11-14). Here is what they draw out of it.

- **Wasting begins with separation.** The first mistake that leads to a wasteful life is separating yourself from God and from fellowship; the prodigal had to journey into a far country before he could waste his substance, because there are certain sins a believer cannot commit while staying in fellowship with the brethren [2].

- **Extravagance is a form of waste.** Living beyond your means and spending in excess is itself a waste of good opportunity, and wasters tend to become poor while those who stop the wastage tend to become rich [1][4].

- **Greed squanders what God has given.** Gehazi was perhaps in line to become the most anointed man of God after Elisha, but that opportunity was denied him because of the spirit of greed, and greed destroyed his ministry and his whole life [5].

- **Wasting costs you your position.** The steward in Luke 16 was called to give an account of his stewardship and told he could no longer be steward; if you waste what God has put in your hand, you lose your privileged position, and God will one day ask you to account for what was in your control [4].

- **Do not despise the small opportunity in front of you.** One man became pastor of a small church in a classroom with only a few young members, and he refused to despise it or throw it away; that opportunity grew in his hands until that little church was in over a hundred countries [6].

- **Do not waste the advice and the pastors God sends you.** Judas had the best counselling, teaching, anointing and example, and wasted it; and many believers treat the humble pastor who ministers to them every Sunday as if he were worth nothing, chasing one sensational prophet after another instead [1][3].

- **Do not waste the opportunity to win souls.** A soul is worth more than all the great cities of the world, and if you lose your chance to win souls while you are on this earth you will regret it for the rest of eternity [3].

- **Above all, do not waste your chance to be saved.** Judas Iscariot was called out by name and had the opportunity to go to Heaven, yet he lost it because he let the devil put betrayal into his heart and would not change his mind despite being warned — and Proverbs 29:1 says that he who is often reproved and hardens his neck will suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy [7].

And if you have already wandered, the books hold out the father's house: if you have the opportunity to eat at table with your Christian family, why

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 1, 4 and 10 of *Opportunities*, chapter 14 of *He That Hath, To Him Shall Be Given: And He That Hath Not, From Him Shall Be Taken Even That Which He Hath*, chapter 24 of *Ready@20* and chapter 38 of *How You Can Preach Salvation*.

Scriptures referenced: 2 Kings 5:27; Proverbs 29:1; Matthew 16:26; Luke 6:12-16; Luke 15:11-14; Luke 16:1-2; John 13:1-2; John 13:27; 1 Thessalonians 5:12-13.

items.question: How should a church deal with sin and rebellion among its leaders?
items.text:
This is a weighty matter, and the books speak to it directly. Here is what they counsel.

- **Do not treat sin lightly.** Many churches fail here, dealing with sin as trivial or not at all, but sin and wickedness must not be allowed to grow until they become an uncontrollable monstrosity [1]. When dismissal, suspension, or removal is required, it must be carried out, or the organization will decline into irreversible corruption [1].

- **Rebellion is its own distinct sin, and it must be rejected.** Rebellion is a specific evil, separate from every other sin — a resistance, disobedience, and defiance of authority [3]. Scripture calls it as the sin of witchcraft (1 Samuel 15:23), and we are told to abhor those in rebellion (Psalm 139:21) and to have nothing to do with them, lest we become rebels ourselves [2][6].

- **Watch for the pattern and the history.** Rebels are described as evil men who seek only rebellion (Proverbs 17:11), defying authority from childhood through adulthood [3]. It is wise to find out about a person's history of rebellion, because such a person moves from one church to another stirring up the same trouble [3].

- **Guard against the slander that follows.** A slanderer is a stubbornly rebellious person (Jeremiah 6:28) who, having rebelled against a leader, seeks to destroy him by speaking maliciously [7]. Watch out for rebellious leavers and disgruntled employees, for they are often your worst slanderers [7].

- **Leaders must be able to judge, which means they must be morally clean themselves.** Judgment and justice establish a church (Proverbs 29:4), but leaders who are themselves deep in immorality cannot pass judgment on the lower ranks, and so perversion thrives and the church is destroyed by inner corruption [8]. A person who lives continually in sin is often in rebellion against God, and that rebellion can turn against any of God's representatives at short notice [5].

- **Combine judgment with pardon.** God combines judgment and restoration well, so we must master both the official rejection of sin and the official pardoning of it [1]. A pardon is the official granting of forgiveness for an offence committed by a bishop, pastor, or church leader [1].

- **Remember that God does not need you to correct His servants.** In the rebellion of Korah, the two hundred and fifty men of renown who joined it perished in the judgment (Numbers 16:34-35), and God wants His children to remember it so they never confront, challenge, or disobey His authority — He can correct His own servants without you [4].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 79 of *The Gift Of Governments*, chapters 5 and 8 of *Those Who Rebel*, chapter 5 of *Loyalty and Disloyalty*, chapter 4 of *How you can become a strong Christian*, chapter 5 of *Those Who Are Slanderers* and chapter 1 of *BEMA Judgment And Justice*.

Scriptures referenced: Numbers 16:34-35; Numbers 16:41-46; Joshua 22:19; Joshua 24:19; 1 Samuel 15:23; 1 Kings 16:31; Ezra 4:19; Nehemiah 9:17; Job 7:21; Job 34:37 and 6 more.

items.question: A member has stopped coming to church and stopped praying. How do I help them come back to God?
items.text:
That's a heavy thing to carry for someone you love, and it's good that you want to go after them.

Praying less is one of the symptoms of backsliding — a Christian who spends less time talking to God is unknowingly moving away from Him, and Jesus said to pray lest you fall into temptation [8]. So the drift in prayer and the drift from church are likely tied together.

Not being committed is another symptom: anyone who does not want to be committed to a church will ultimately leave that church, and an uncommitted Christian is a potential backslider [8]. God expects the believer to be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, and every Christian must be planted in the house of the Lord — you need to belong somewhere [8].

Staying in fellowship is itself a key to receiving the Lord's blessings. As 1 John 1:7 says, if we walk in the light we have fellowship one with another — so if you are in the light, you will go to church and fellowship with other Christians [3].

And when they do come back, travail for them in prayer, as Galatians 4:19 puts it, until Christ is formed in them — pray that they will become established in Christ [6].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 9 of *How to Pray*, chapter 10 of *The Mega Church* and chapter 7 of *Backsliding*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 119:133; Proverbs 7:10; Galatians 4:19; 1 John 1:7; 1 John 3:22.

items.question: How do I stay filled with the Holy Spirit?
items.book: The Sweet Influences of the Anointing
items.text:
Staying filled with the Holy Spirit is something you keep doing, not something you finish once. Here is how the books describe it.

- **Ask for Him, again and again.** Jesus told us to pray for the Holy Spirit, and the Father gives Him to those who ask (Luke 11:13) [1][4]. You never reach a point where you have enough of Him; there are always further measures, gifts and impartations to receive [1].

- **Talk and preach about Him.** Talking about the Holy Spirit stirs up hunger and interest in the things of the Spirit, and the blessing of being hungry is that you will be filled (Matthew 5:6) [4].

- **Pray together with others.** The early church was filled with the Holy Spirit when they prayed together, and every prayer meeting brings down His presence [1].

- **Speak to yourself in psalms, hymns and spiritual songs.** Ephesians 5:18-19 tells us to be filled with the Spirit by speaking to ourselves in songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord [1][2]. The songs that fill you must come from the heart, not hastily written words meant to impress [2].

- **Be thankful, always and for all things.** Ephesians 5:18-20 ties being filled with the Spirit to giving thanks always for all things [2][3]. Thankfulness opens you to the Spirit, while criticism and murmuring open you to evil spirits [2][3].

- **Stay humble and submitted to one another.** Ephesians 5:18-21 ends the same passage with submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God, and being filled with the Spirit is closely linked to humility and submissiveness toward others [2].

- **Keep your spirit full of good things.** Empty Christians are targets for the enemy, because a vacuum will be filled with something (Luke 11:25) [7][8]. Fill your spirit with the Word of God, with faith, with good Christian music, and fill your time with church activities, so that emptiness is driven out [7][8].

- **Relate to Him as a real person.** You can talk to the Holy Spirit, greet Him, discuss things with Him, and listen for His advice, recognizing His thoughts and ideas [5]. You can also recognize Him as wind — the gentle pressures, the sudden gusts, the sense of being enveloped [5].

- **Let Him revive, satisfy, refresh and grow you.** The Spirit is like water: He revives you in dry places (Isaiah 44:3-4), satisfies you (Psalm 36:8), refreshes you (Psalm 63:1), and makes you like a watered garden where everything grows (Isaiah 58:11) [6].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 31 of *The Sweet Influences of the Anointing*, chapter 3 of *Those Who Forget*, chapters 1 and 7 of *Flow in the Anointing*, chapter 2 of *How you can become a strong Christian* and chapter 3 of *Backsliding*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 36:8; Psalms 63:1; Isaiah 44:3-4; Isaiah 58:11; Matthew 5:6; Luke 11:13; Luke 11:25; John 20:22; Acts 2:2; Acts 4:31 and 10 more.

items.question: What does the Bible say about pastors criticizing or attacking other pastors and ministries?
items.book: The Church Must Send or It Will End
items.text:
The books speak to this plainly, and with one voice: this is a serious matter, and it grieves the Body of Christ.

- **It is destructive, not building.** When pastors deride and denigrate other ministers, they are tearing down the very Body they claim to serve; the most wicked and destructive statements about the Body of Christ have come from pastors themselves, who ridicule one another privately and from their pulpits, then mount those same pulpits on Sunday to try to build what they destroyed during the week [4]. The counsel is direct: do not break down somebody's house in order to build yours, and do not break down someone else's church to build yours, for you will reap what you sow [4].

- **It is a danger sign in a minister.** Attacking and killing your own brother is a very bad sign and a cause for concern, and you must recognize the danger signs of ministers who attack other colleagues [3]. Many pastors do not realize that most of their discussions centre on others rather than on the Word of God, and constant analysis, criticism and mockery of fellow ministers is most common in the conversation of some pastors [3]. The writer notes he has found himself drawing away from the company of such ministers [3].

- **It is a snare that can end your own ministry.** Cain received a withering curse when he attacked and killed his own brother (Genesis 4:8-12), and many pastors attack their fellow pastors instead of concentrating on the work of ministry that lies undone [2]. The counsel is to leave other ministers to God, for His judgment is greater than your criticism, and your own ministry can come to an end because of your attack on another person's ministry [2].

- **It is a mark of rebellion against God's servants.** Rebellion can be against the Lord and His servants, and many times when you are defying God's servants you are defying God Himself [6]. Disobeying God's servant is rebellion, and you are told to abhor those in rebellion and have nothing to do with them, lest you become a rebel yourself [6].

- **It invites a curse, and God defends His servants.** A curse is activated against all who attack their fathers in the ministry, and the prophecy of Isaiah 41 protects God's servants: those incensed against them shall be ashamed and confounded, and those who strive with them shall perish [5]. The word of God cannot be broken, and your ministry will come to an end when you have a bad relationship with your father [5].

- **The right focus is the harvest, not each other.** Instead of attacking one another, pastors are to concentrate on the Great Commission and on how to go to the ends of the earth, so that all can join in the harvest of souls [2]. The instruction given to the captains of Syria was to fight neither with small nor great, but only with the king of Israel

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 4 and 8 of *The Church Must Send or It Will End*, chapter 8 of *Those who are Dangerous Sons*, chapter 3 of *Those Who Are Ignorant* and chapter 8 of *Those Who Rebel*.

Scriptures referenced: Genesis 4:8-12; Joshua 22:19; 2 Samuel 13:28; 2 Samuel 14:28; Nehemiah 9:17; Psalms 139:21.

- **The right focus is the harvest, not each other.** Instead of attacking one another, pastors are to concentrate on the Great Commission and on how to go to the ends of the earth, so that all can join in the harvest of souls.

items.question: A leader I trained for years has just left the church. How do I handle it?
items.text:
That is a deep wound, and I am sorry you are carrying it. Let me walk through what our books say about handling a departure like this.

First, let your own heart be cleansed. When someone leaves, it pollutes your spirit with seeds of hurt, anger, hatred, wickedness and revenge, and you will need to pray long and hard to get free of them, or you will fall into bitterness and unforgiveness [4]. David prayed to be kept from the snares of those who do iniquity, asking that the wicked fall into their own nets while he passed by safely (Psalm 141:9-10) [4].

Then deal with the person quickly and decisively. If anyone indicates a desire to resign, it is best for such a person not to stay but to leave immediately, because his heart has already left the church [7]. One dissenting person pollutes the others with his disgruntled attitude, for "a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump" (1 Corinthians 5:6), and when Judas resigned from Jesus' ministry, Jesus told him, "That thou doest, do quickly" (John 13:27) [7]. Binding a "Judas" means restricting him; some leaders let such people operate freely even after they know they are disloyal, and that is one of the great mistakes of leadership [2].

Watch for the domino effect. When one pastor's departure causes a series of other departures, an evil domino spirit has been released into your ministry [1]. Bishop Dag Heward-Mills tells of a Boeing 747 pilot he trained into a pastor, who broke away and started an independent church near the one he had led; a few years later, several pastors from his former team left one after another and started splinter churches, dotting the city with them and leaving hundreds of confused members [1]. The first breakaway set the example, and the others said to themselves, "If he can do that we can do that too" [1].

Dispel the confusion with the Word. Many who leave release a spirit of confusion, and God is not its author — "God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints" (1 Corinthians 14:33) [4]. items.question: What does it mean to be a shepherd over a small group of people?
items.book: What It Means to Become a Shepherd
items.text:
Being a shepherd over a small group means you are a caring, loving guide to those sheep — someone God has called to look after them [3]. It is not a title but a job: you have time to care, time to love, time to feed and time to gather the sheep [1].

It is a great honour to be chosen from among men for this, and to be given a job in things pertaining to God [2]. You are also privileged to help people prosper, to provide good food for them, and to lead them [4].

Concretely, that means you lead your sheep by still waters and to green pastures, you guide them through wilderness situations, and you lead them like a flock — learning to lead people with diverse opinions and backgrounds, even in the face of opposition from independent sheep and rebellious people [5]. You minister one-on-one to them, because a man may preach to thousands but cannot personally talk to thousands [6]. You keep the church family together, and you notice the problems of your sheep — knowing when they are doing exams, when they are having marital problems [7]. You share the burden of praying, visiting, counselling and interacting with the sheep, and you will also give an account for each soul God gave you [8].

And it begins with love: Jesus told Peter to prove his love by feeding and caring for the sheep — "Peter, do you love me? If you love me feed my sheep!" [3].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapters 1, 2, 5 and 13 of *What It Means to Become a Shepherd*, chapters 2 and 3 of *The Privilege* and chapter 20 of *The Art of Shepherding*.

Scriptures referenced: Psalms 23:1-2; Psalms 77:20; Psalms 78:52-54; Psalms 95:6-7; Ezekiel 34:5; Matthew 9:36; John 10:12; John 21:15-17.

items.question: How can a pastor's wife support her husband's ministry if she's quiet and doesn't connect with people?
items.book: The Beauty The Beast and The Pastor
items.text:
That's a real tension, and I'm glad you asked it plainly.

A wife who is helpful is a quiet and effective backbone to any minister, and many ministers depend on their wives for exactly that kind of quiet help [1]. Quietness itself is not the problem — salt works quietly and effectively, and the helps ministry is a behind-the-scenes ministry where great helpers are often unseen and unknown by the general public [1]. So a pastor's wife can be the salt of the earth by being a quiet and effective helps minister, and jobs like being a prayer warrior or a secretary are quiet and effective ways of having influence [1].

But the books also treat isolation and non-communicative behaviour as a serious flaw, not a personality trait to hide behind. To be non-communicative is a serious flaw in your ministry, and to be isolated is a serious mistake in ministry [4]. Those who are non-communicative rarely do well in ministry; they may say they are naturally quiet, but that is a smoke screen for a serious flaw [4]. You will never be made perfect without the input of others — as Hebrews 11:40 says, "they without us should not be made perfect" — and no member can say to another, "I have no need of thee" (1 Corinthians 12:20-21) [4]. The body increases through what every joint supplies [4].

So the two books are speaking to two different things: quiet, hidden, faithful service is honoured [1], while withdrawing from connection with others is warned against [4]. If the quietness is the quietness of salt — praying, helping, giving without needing to be seen — that is a gift to your husband's ministry [1]. If it has become isolation, the books say plainly that your church will not work without the input of other people, other ministers, and other churches [4].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 10 of *Am I Good For Nothing?* and chapter 4 of *Why Is This Church Not Working?*.

Scriptures referenced: Genesis 2:18; Matthew 6:3-4; Romans 12:8; 1 Corinthians 12:20-21; 1 Corinthians 12:28; Hebrews 11:40.
