items.question: What should I do when one of them is a leader I trained?
items.text:
That is a particular kind of pain — you gave yourself to training someone, and now they are the one leaving. Let me give you what the books say.

**Let them go without a fight.** When a person departs, you are not to hold them back or chase them; the counsel is to release them and let God deal with the matter [1]. David did not hunt Saul down when Saul's heart departed from the Lord — he waited on God, and God revealed the man after His own heart in His own time [5].

**Do not let them take others with them.** If a leader you trained is leaving, they must not influence other ministers or members to leave with them [1]. They should resign alone, and they should discourage others from following them [1]. When a pastor broke away from Bishop Dag's church, he had spent time influencing the people first, and he led away about eighty percent of the congregation [6]. That is the pattern to guard against.

**Require them to declare their intentions openly and early.** Anyone intending to leave should declare it long beforehand, and if they plan to set up a church, they must declare that intention to the senior minister [1]. This is precisely so that the members are not left confused, having to choose between their relationship with the one leaving and their commitment to the church [1].

**Keep them from planting right next to you.** The counsel is that a departing person should not set up a church anywhere within a ten-mile radius of where they used to be [1]. When one pastor started his own church near the one he had been in charge of, despite persistent warnings, several of his fellow pastors later followed his example, and soon the city was dotted with splinter churches and hundreds of confused members who did not know which group to belong to [7].

**Do not retaliate, and do not speak evil of them.** You are to be grateful to the church you came from and not spread bad stories after leaving [1] — and the same spirit applies to how you handle those who leave you. Scripture says, "Whoso rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house" (Proverbs 17:13) [1]. Speaking evil muddies the waters you once drank from, and Ezekiel 34:18 rebukes those who foul the residue of the pasture with their feet [1].

**Guard your own heart against presumption.** Moses rebuked Korah for presumption — the arrogant assumption of privilege — because Korah was a Levite and a leader of the congregation, yet spoke rudely to the servant of God (Numbers 16:3, 16:8-9) [2]. A trained leader who turns and speaks rudely to those above him is showing that same spirit [2].

**Trust God to replace them.** Sometimes the departure of a person heralds the arrival of God's choice for you [5]. When a worship leader Bishop Dag

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 10 of *Loyalty and Disloyalty*, chapter 4 of *Those Who Forget* and chapters 3, 5 and 10 of *Those who leave you*.

Scriptures referenced: Numbers 16:3; Numbers 16:8-9; 1 Kings 12:28-31; Proverbs 17:13; Ezekiel 34:18.

items.question: What happens to a person who dies without being born again?
items.text:
This is one of the most sobering questions any of us can ask, and our books speak to it plainly.

When a person dies without being born again, they do not simply stop existing or become nothing. They head for a permanent destination away from this earth — either Heaven or Hell — and the one who dies unsaved goes to Hell [4]. Jesus told of a rich man and a beggar named Lazarus: the beggar died and was carried by angels into Abraham's bosom, while the rich man died, was buried, and in Hell lifted up his eyes in torments [4]. The rich man's soul could still remember, think, and feel as though he were on earth, and it was his soul that suffered in the flame [7].

The reason is that sin entered the world through one man, Adam, and death spread to all men because all sinned, as Romans 5:12 says; this passed a death sentence on all of us and made every unsaved soul an automatic candidate for Hell [2]. It is not even something a person has to work at — even just sitting still and minding your own business, you would still end up there [2]. The unsaved person is spiritually dead, separated from a holy God, just as the dead are separated from the living; unless a man is born again and reconciled to God through Christ, he is headed for Hell [2].

So the condition is serious, and it is why the question of being born again matters so much. But the door is not shut while a person is still alive: being born again is simple — believe in Jesus Christ as the Son of God, as 1 John 5:1 says, and ask Him to come into your heart and life, repenting of your sins and receiving Him as Lord and Saviour [8].

Bishop Dag Heward-Mills talks about this in chapter 11 of *People Who Went to Hell*, chapters 3 and 4 of *How to be Born again & Avoid Hell* and chapter 1 of *Key Facts for New Believers*.

Scriptures referenced: Jeremiah 17:9; Ezekiel 36:26-27; Mark 8:36; Luke 16:19-31; Romans 1:18; Romans 5:12; 1 John 5:1.
